title: Streaming Hierarchical Inference with Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.07956v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) have recently demonstrated strong predictive performance through in-context learning, but their deployment in high-throughput data streams remains challenging due to communication overhead and latency. We propose \textit{HINT}, a hierarchical inference framework that combines edge-based retrieval with cloud-based TFM inference. A graph-based approximate nearest neighbor memory maintained over a sliding window provides local predictions and uncertainty estimates, allowing confident samples to be processed locally while uncertain instances are selectively offloaded, together with their retrieved context, to a cloud-hosted TFM. The framework exposes an offloading threshold and a neighborhood retrieval policy that can be varied to balance predictive performance and communication cost. Experiments show \textit{HINT} consistently identifies favorable trade-offs.

translated_title: 基于表格基础模型的流式分层推理
translated_abstract: 表格基础模型（TFMs）近期通过上下文学习展现出了强大的预测性能，但由于通信开销和延迟问题，其在高吞吐量数据流中的部署仍然充满挑战。我们提出了 HINT，一种将基于边缘的检索与基于云的 TFM 推理相结合的分层推理框架。该框架在滑动窗口上维护一个基于图的近似最近邻记忆，提供本地预测和不确定性估计，使高置信度样本能够在本地处理，而不确定的实例则连同其检索到的上下文被选择性地卸载至云端托管的 TFM。该框架提供了一个卸载阈值和一个邻域检索策略，可通过调节二者来平衡预测性能与通信成本。实验表明，HINT 能够持续找到有利的权衡点。
tldr: HINT 提出了一种边缘-云协同的分层推理框架，通过滑动窗口上的图近似最近邻记忆在本地进行预测与不确定性估计，仅将不确定的样本连同检索上下文卸载到云端表格基础模型，从而在预测性能与通信成本之间实现有效平衡。
